data.gender_notes: Brad is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Old English name Bradan or Brada comes from the Old English words brad and dæg meaning broad and wide, or broad-shouldered. In Old English literature, Brad was a common name for warriors and strong men. The name Brad carries the meaning “Broad, wide, or strong” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Brad usually hope their child will grow to embody broad, wide, or strong and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Brad
in_english.meaning: Brad is a short form of Bradley, meaning broad or wide meadow
in_english.long_meaning: The name Brad, often a diminutive form of Bradley, originates from Old English words 'brad' meaning broad and 'leah' meaning meadow or clearing. It symbolizes a wide or broad meadow, often associated with openness and fertility. While not directly mentioned in the Bible, the concept of broad or wide spaces can be seen in biblical references to open fields and meadows, symbolizing freedom and abundance. Historically, the name has been used in Christian traditions to signify expansive landscapes and open-heartedness.

data.cultural_impact: The name Brad was common in Anglo-Saxon England and continues to be popular due to its strong association with strength, courage, and masculinity. Numerous well-known individuals with the name Brad, including actors Brad Pitt and Brad Garrett, further reinforce these characteristics.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Brad, with its origins in the Old English language, plays a subtle yet significant role in spiritual contemplation. It serves as a reminder of the strength and breadth of God's character, encompassing both mercy and justice. The name Brad, in its meaning of broad and wide, can also be seen as a reflection of the breadth and depth of God's love and wisdom.
